newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-ELLIOTT RETIRES HURT AFTER COLLISION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ELLIOTT RETIRES HURT AFTER COLLISION.

text.p: Opener Matthew Elliott was forced to retire hurt after scoring his maiden test half-century as Australia tightened their grip on the second test against West Indies on Monday.
Elliott took an important step to secure his immediate test future with an unbeaten 78 before being involved in a painful collision with batting partner Mark Waugh just before lunch.
Elliott, who hurt his knee in the incident, held his side's second innings together as Australia built a substantial lead of 171 runs with eight wickets in hand at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
At lunch on the fourth day, Australia were 144 for two, with Waugh on 31 not out alongside Michael Bevan on one.
Elliott and Waugh collided as they were sprinting between the wickets for a second run with the total on 143 for two.

Although both batsmen were knocked to the ground, Elliott managed to dive back to the safety of his crease, foiling West Indies' attempt to run him out. But he was unable to carry on batting after lengthy treatment.
Australia struggled for runs on a slow wicket, adding 67 runs during the session after starting the day on 77 for two.
With five sessions left to play, Australia are expected to bat until at least tea, leaving the West Indies to chase a target of about 300 or, more realistically, bat out the fifth day to earn a draw.
West Indies scored 304 in their first innings in reply to Australia's 331.
Elliott was selected for the first test in Brisbane as a replacement for Michael Slater, who was left out because of poor form.
Although Australia won the test by 123 runs, Elliott struggled badly, losing his wicket cheaply in both innings in a nervous display.
